content:
I made this diagram to summarize a key Kaggriculture relationship: an opponent can change your result without directly attacking your farm.

Core relationship

Opponent action Shared effect Competitive impact
Sells goods Market inventory rises Prices can fall
Changes production mix Future supply changes Fixed plans may be mistimed
Builds a stronger bank Comparison target rises Higher income may still lose
Changes the match result Rating update changes Evaluation depends on the field

Opponent actions -> shared inventory -> market prices -> your decisions -> final bank comparison -> match result -> rating update

Practical takeaway

Kaggriculture is an adaptation problem, not only a single-farm optimization problem. A useful local evaluation should include:

  • several opponent archetypes;
  • both seats and multiple seeds;
  • market-contention scenarios;
  • final bank balance as well as win rate;
  • checks for policies that win self-play but fail against a different supply mix.

The attached diagram stays at the game-mechanics level and excludes private agent names, code, submission IDs, and exact thresholds.

How are you modeling opponent-driven market effects in your evaluation?

Suggested evaluation matrix

Axis Minimum useful coverage
Opponents Multiple production styles
Positions Both player seats
Randomness Several fixed seeds
Market pressure Similar and different goods
Metrics Wins, bank balance, and variance

This is a conceptual interpretation for discussion, not an organizer ruling. I would be interested in examples where the same policy changes behavior after observing shared inventory or expected supply.
